aspects.says: collect(supplier, accumulator, combiner) gives each chunk its own container from the supplier, and its combiner must merge two containers fully.
basis: section:reduce Combines Values; a Mutable Container Goes Through collect

aspects.says: The three-argument reduce's combiner is not called on a sequential stream in the JDK, so a combiner that disagrees with the accumulator passes sequential tests and gives wrong results in parallel.
basis: section:The Three-Argument Form's Combiner Runs Only on a Parallel Stream

aspects.says: findAny may return any match and on a parallel stream varies between runs; findFirst returns the first match in encounter order on an ordered stream.
basis: section:findAny Is Free to Return Any Match

aspects.says: groupingBy's downstream collector decides what each group becomes (counting counts elements, mapping to a set keeps distinct values), and its map has no promised type or order unless a map factory such as TreeMap::new is given.
basis: section:groupingBy Gives a Map of Lists in No Promised Order; a Downstream and a Map Factory Change Both

aspects.says: reduce's identity must leave every element unchanged, because a parallel stream starts every chunk from it; a value such as a fee used as identity is added once per chunk.
basis: section:reduce Needs an Identity That Changes Nothing and an Operation That Can Be Regrouped

aspects.says: joining with a prefix and suffix returns prefix + suffix for an empty stream.
basis: section:teeing Feeds Two Collectors in One Pass, and joining Writes Its Prefix Even for Nothing

aspects.says: A mutable container passed to reduce as identity is one object shared by every chunk, so a parallel reduce into it loses, duplicates or throws.
basis: section:reduce Combines Values; a Mutable Container Goes Through collect

aspects.says: reduce's operation must be associative; a running subtraction gives the right answer sequentially and a different one in parallel.
basis: section:reduce Needs an Identity That Changes Nothing and an Operation That Can Be Regrouped

aspects.says: reduce with an identity returns the identity for an empty stream, so a sentinel becomes a plausible wrong value; reduce without one, min, max, findFirst and findAny return an Optional that is empty for an empty stream.
basis: section:Without an Identity, reduce Returns an Optional, and So Do min, max and findFirst

aspects.says: partitioningBy always has both the true and the false key; groupingBy by a predicate has only the keys some element mapped to, so a missing group reads as null.
basis: section:partitioningBy Always Has Both Keys; groupingBy Has Only the Keys It Saw

aspects.says: Collectors.teeing sends every element to two collectors and merges their results.
basis: section:teeing Feeds Two Collectors in One Pass, and joining Writes Its Prefix Even for Nothing
aspects.reason: whether a result came from one pass or two cannot be observed by a test, and the result itself is what the downstream collectors already give; the page shows the run

aspects.says: Stream.toList() is unmodifiable and keeps nulls, Collectors.toList() promises no mutability (an ArrayList in Java 21), and toUnmodifiableList() throws NullPointerException on a null.
basis: section:toList(), Collectors.toList() and toUnmodifiableList() Return Three Different Lists

aspects.says: toArray() returns Object[], and casting it to String[] throws ClassCastException; toArray(String[]::new) returns a String[].
basis: section:toList(), Collectors.toList() and toUnmodifiableList() Return Three Different Lists
